messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P0 created for HelioCorp (VPC tenant). Symptom: sudden KV prefix hit-rate collapse in tenant-specific cache causing ~10x CPU on their dedicated retriever pool and 503s for generation endpoints. Pager: @Alice R.

Alice R.: seeing spike in error rates and timeouts from HelioCorp's VPC pool. Metrics: prefix_hitrate down from 0.91 -> 0.08 in ~12m. Appears isolated to tenant prefixes; global cache looks fine. Paging oncall.

Marc T.: joining. quick checks: which nodes host their prefixes? running `kubectl get pods -l app=kv-cache -o wide` to map. Also pulling top keys: `redis-cli --scan | grep helio:` (they use per-tenant prefix).

Alice R.: logs show lots of SETs for random-looking prefixes from their app. Possibly cache pollution or a replication storm after a failover.

Yang (eng-ml): could be model-side client misconfig; we've seen client that accidentally rotates prefixes per-request. But 10x CPU suggests hot churn. Any change in client rollout?

Sam (Support): HelioCorp reports a deploy ~15m before incident, released by their infra team. They said nothing touched LLM routing, but they increased parallel requests.

Jenny L.: assigned SRE lead. Plan: 1) throttle HelioCorp to reduce write pressure, 2) pin fallback to cold model to reduce CPU, 3) temporarily disable prefix prefetch for their tenant, 4) roll caches to evict pollution. Who can run tenant throttles?

Alice R.: I can apply rate-limit on the tenant route via gateway. Command: `redwoodctl route update --tenant helio --max-qps 80` (reduces burst). Doing it now.

deploy-bot: route update applied by alice.rivera at 2005012402.

Marc T.: initiating cache isolation step. We'll flip the tenant's cache mode to "bypass writable" so SETs go to fallback DB but don't populate the shared prefix cache. Command I will run on cache control plane: `cachectl tenant-set helio write_mode=pass-through`

Marc T.: Running `cachectl tenant-set helio write_mode=pass-through`... done. Observing metrics.

Alice R.: early signal: write throughput dropped ~70%, CPU on retriever pool trending down. Error rate still elevated due to prior pollution causing misses and backend pressure.

Yang (eng-ml): recommend disabling prefetch of KV for HelioCorp for now. Prefetch is adding loads of extra keys. How to toggle?

Marc T.: `cachectl tenant-set helio prefetch.enabled=false` — turning off.

Marc T.: prefetch disabled. Also initiating targeted eviction of top noisy prefixes: `cachectl evict --tenant helio --pattern 'helio:tmp:*'`

Alice R.: eviction command ran. Monitoring hit-rate: from 0.08 -> 0.27 within 4m. Not back to normal yet.

Sam (Support): notified HelioCorp PS and provided mitigation steps and ETA. They're appreciative but asking for an ETA to restore normal traffic.

Lina - AM: pls keep me posted; customer is in contact with security and infra. They want a rollback plan if things worsen.

Jenny L.: escalations: if hit-rate <0.5 in 20m, we consider rolling redeploy of cache nodes hosting their shard with fresh state. Also evaluate enabling tenant-local in-memory cache (temporary) to serve reads while writes are bypassed.

incident-bot: On-call handoff reminder: Alice R. is primary until 2005013000 UTC; Jenny L. is coordinating.

Marc T.: I can do a graceful restart of the 3 cache pods that host their shard. Doing one at a time with drain to avoid cold start storm. Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -l shard=helio-shard-3 --timeout=5m`

deploy-bot: restart initiated by marc.t at 2005012460 on pod kv-cache-3a -> draining connections.

Alice R.: added a temporary fallback routing rule: route HelioCorp -> smaller model variant to reduce per-request CPU: `redwoodctl routing set --tenant helio --model gpt-slim-8k` This will lower cost/perf but reduce pressure.

Yang (eng-ml): note we may see higher token count due to different prompt handling in slim model; watch for function outputs. We'll create an eval gate for HelioCorp sample prompts.

Marc T.: restart completed for pod 3a, hit-rate improved further to 0.42. Restarting pod 3b next. Doing rolling now.

Alice R.: customer-facing status update drafted: "We've identified a client-side deploy causing excessive unique KV prefixes create. We've applied rate-limits and disabled tenant prefetch; rolling cache restarts in progress. Next update in 30m." Sam, can you send?

Sam (Support): sent to HelioCorp at 2005012502. They acknowledged and paused their deploy. Good signal.

Marc T.: all 3 cache pods rotated. Current prefix_hitrate 0.68 — trending toward baseline but still catching up. CPU back to normal range.

Jenny L.: next steps: 1) keep bypass write_mode for 1 hour, 2) keep prefetch disabled until customer confirms fix, 3) coordinate postmortem and client-side recommendations (avoid per-request rotating prefixes, use bounded key-space). Assigning postmortem owner: Marc T.

Lina - AM: customer wants written summary and timeline. Sam please include timeline and mitigations.

Sam (Support): will compile and share draft by EOD.

Alice R.: resolving pager for now but leaving incident open for monitoring. If we see reversion, we'll page back.

incident-bot: INCIDENT status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident P0 -> P1. Created incident ticket INC-2005012345.

Jenny L.: thanks team — great coordination. Marc, please include config diffs and `cachectl` commands in the postmortem so ops runbook is clear.

Marc T.: will produce runbook + timeline. Adding quick mitigation snippet for future: ```
# mitigation checklist (helio pattern)
redwoodctl route update --tenant <tenant> --max-qps 80
cachectl tenant-set <tenant> write_mode=pass-through
cachectl tenant-set <tenant> prefetch.enabled=false
cachectl evict --tenant <tenant> --pattern '<tenant>:tmp:*'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/kv-cache -l shard=<shard-id> --timeout=5m
redwoodctl routing set --tenant <tenant> --model <fallback-model>
```

Alice R.: leaving a note: ensure we add an alert that flags tenant-specific SET:GET ratio > 5x baseline; that'll catch pollution earlier.

Jenny L.: agreed. I'll own alert creation after postmortem. Closing out chronology here; last check-in in 30m.

Sam (Support): HelioCorp confirmed reduced errors and resumed limited traffic.

Alice R.: last check at 2005012520: prefix_hitrate 0.83 and error rate stabilized. marking last_message_ts.
